summary:
AGRIHORIZON is an intelligent, climate-smart agricultural decision-support platform that transforms Earth-observation data and agricultural information into practical insights for farmers. Developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data,” AGRIHORIZON connects relevant environmental observations with local farm conditions, available soil information, crop characteristics and farmer-defined priorities to support informed agricultural planning and crop-rotation decisions.

Through farm monitoring, environmental analysis, crop and rotation exploration, and AI-assisted guidance, it helps users examine changing temperature and rainfall patterns, consider potential agricultural risks, and compare crop options and rotation strategies suited to local conditions.

Rather than simply displaying data, AGRIHORIZON aims to make complex scientific information understandable and useful in everyday farming decisions. By supporting informed crop planning, soil-conscious practices, responsible resource management and climate preparedness, it seeks to contribute to more resilient farming systems, healthier soils, improved harvest potential and stronger livelihoods for farming communities worldwide. 
The future of agriculture depends not only on understanding our changing planet, but also on turning that knowledge into meaningful action.

AGRIHORIZON — SEE BEYOND. GROW SMARTER.

01. PROJECT OVERVIEW

AGRIHORIZON: SEE BEYOND. GROW SMARTER.

Transforming Earth-observation science into meaningful agricultural decisions.

Agriculture is one of humanity's most essential systems, yet its future increasingly depends on how effectively farming communities understand and respond to changing environmental conditions. Temperature variations, unpredictable rainfall, water availability, soil degradation and changing crop suitability create interconnected challenges that demand more informed and adaptable agricultural decisions.

AGRIHORIZON is an intelligent, climate-smart agricultural decision-support platform developed by INKINDI TECH in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data."

The project seeks to bridge the gap between Earth-observation science and practical agricultural decision-making. It connects environmental observations with geographical farm information, available soil data, crop characteristics and farmer-defined priorities to help users understand their agricultural environments and explore crop suitability and crop-rotation strategies adapted to local conditions.

Rather than simply displaying satellite images, weather information or isolated agricultural statistics, AGRIHORIZON aims to bring these different sources of information together within one accessible digital environment. Through farm monitoring, environmental analysis, crop and rotation exploration, and AI-assisted agricultural guidance, the platform is designed to transform complex information into understandable insights that can support more informed farming decisions.Figure 1. AGRIHORIZON's original web application interface, developed by INKINDI TECH, illustrating the platform's approach to connecting agricultural information and environmental intelligence.

A GLOBAL VISION, ADAPTABLE TO LOCAL REALITIES

AGRIHORIZON is conceived as a globally adaptable solution for farming communities across different continents, climates, soil conditions and agricultural systems. Its approach recognizes that no two agricultural environments are identical: meaningful decisions must consider geographical conditions, crop requirements, available resources and the priorities of the people who cultivate the land.

OUR CENTRAL PURPOSE

To make Earth-observation information and agricultural knowledge more accessible, understandable and actionable, helping farmers explore sustainable crop choices, consider soil health, prepare for environmental changes and make better-informed decisions.

AGRIHORIZON represents our vision of agriculture in which scientific intelligence and human knowledge work together to support more resilient farming systems, healthier soils, improved harvest potential and stronger agricultural livelihoods.

AGRIHORIZON — SEE BEYOND. GROW SMARTER.

Developed by INKINDI TECH
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

02. THE GLOBAL AGRICULTURAL CHALLENGE

2.1 Agriculture in a Changing Climate

Agriculture depends on environmental conditions that are becoming increasingly difficult to predict. Temperature changes, shifting rainfall patterns, prolonged dry periods, extreme heat and intense rainfall can affect planting schedules, crop development, water availability and harvest outcomes. These pressures do not affect every region in the same way, but they create growing challenges for agricultural planning worldwide.

The World Meteorological Organization reported that 2025 was approximately 1.43°C above the 1850–1900 average, making it the second or third warmest year in the observational record. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has also reported that climate change has slowed the growth of global agricultural productivity over the past 50 years. This demonstrates why agricultural decisions increasingly need to consider both present environmental conditions and longer-term climate trends.

2.2 Soil Degradation and Water Pressure

Climate is only part of the challenge. Healthy soil and reliable water resources are essential foundations of agricultural production, yet they face significant pressure from unsustainable land management, erosion, land-use changes and increasing demand.

According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), more than 1.6 billion hectares of land have been degraded by unsustainable land-use and management practices. More than 60% of this degradation occurs on agricultural land, including cropland and pasture. FAO also reports that agriculture accounts for more than 70% of global freshwater withdrawals.

These figures highlight the importance of protecting soil, managing water responsibly and considering the long-term effects of agricultural practices. Crop selection and rotation are therefore not simply seasonal choices; they can form part of a wider approach to maintaining productive and resilient farming systems.

2.3 The Information-to-Decision Gap

Scientific observations, satellite imagery, climate records and soil information can help explain changing environmental conditions. However, these sources do not automatically provide a farmer with a clear answer to practical questions:

  • What environmental conditions are affecting my farming area?
  • What risks should I consider when planning the next growing season?
  • Which crop options are worth exploring under the available conditions?
  • How could different crop-rotation strategies support soil health?
  • How can I compare possible choices while considering my own priorities and resources?

The challenge is not simply a lack of data. It is the difficulty of connecting different types of information, understanding their limitations and translating them into decisions that reflect local realities.

2.4 Why Better Agricultural Decision Support Matters

Farmers operate in different climates, landscapes, soil conditions and economic circumstances. A recommendation that may be appropriate in one region cannot automatically be applied to another. Effective agricultural planning therefore needs to consider location, available environmental evidence, soil information, crop characteristics and the farmer's own priorities.

This is the challenge AGRIHORIZON addresses. The platform aims to bring relevant Earth-observation information and agricultural knowledge into one accessible decision-support experience, helping users understand environmental conditions, explore crop and rotation options, and make more informed plans.

The need is global: turn complex environmental information into understandable, locally relevant agricultural insight.

03. THE PROPOSED SOLUTION — INTRODUCING AGRIHORIZON

3.1 Introducing AGRIHORIZON

AGRIHORIZON is a climate-smart agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers and agricultural users better understand their land, interpret environmental conditions and explore informed farming strategies.

Developed by INKINDI TECH in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, the platform brings together relevant Earth-observation information, geographic context, available soil information, crop characteristics and farmer-defined priorities within one accessible digital experience.

Its central idea is to bridge the gap between scientific environmental information and practical agricultural planning.

3.2 How the Solution Addresses the Challenge

AGRIHORIZON approaches agricultural planning through four connected elements:

1. Understand the environment

The platform presents relevant environmental information, including temperature, rainfall and other available climate indicators. This helps users explore the environmental conditions affecting a selected agricultural area.

2. Understand the land

Geographic and available soil information provide additional context about farming locations. Satellite-derived observations and other relevant datasets can help users examine land conditions and vegetation patterns, while recognizing the limitations of each source.

3. Explore crop and rotation strategies

The crop and rotation planning experience helps users examine crop options and compare possible rotation strategies in relation to environmental conditions, available soil information, crop characteristics and their priorities.

4. Turn information into understandable guidance

The AI Farm Advisor is designed to make agricultural information easier to understand by helping users interpret available insights, explore questions and consider possible actions. Its guidance is decision support, not a guarantee of crop performance or a replacement for local agricultural expertise.

3.3 One Connected Agricultural Intelligence Experience

Rather than requiring users to navigate separate sources of environmental and agricultural information, AGRIHORIZON brings relevant insights together through connected platform features:

  • Farm Overview: A central view of farm information and key agricultural indicators.
  • Farm Mapping: Geographic exploration of selected agricultural locations.
  • Farm Intelligence: Environmental information and available satellite-derived insights.
  • Crop and Rotation Planner: Exploration and comparison of crop choices and rotation strategies.
  • AI Farm Advisor: AI-assisted explanations and agricultural guidance.
  • Alerts and Field Guidance: A space for communicating relevant risks, changes and suggested preventive considerations.
  • Learning Centre: Agricultural learning resources designed to make useful knowledge more accessible.

3.4 Designed for Different Farming Regions

Agricultural conditions vary across continents, countries and individual farms. AGRIHORIZON is therefore designed around location-aware information rather than assuming that one recommendation works everywhere.

Users should be able to explore agricultural information relevant to their selected locations, while the platform considers differences in climate, soil information, crop suitability and farming priorities.

Its long-term vision is to make scientific agricultural intelligence more accessible to farming communities worldwide, including communities with limited access to complex technical information.

3.5 The Expected Value of the Solution

By connecting environmental observations with agricultural context and decision-support tools, AGRIHORIZON aims to help users:

  • Better understand changing environmental conditions.
  • Explore potential agricultural risks.
  • Compare possible crop choices and rotation strategies.
  • Consider soil health and responsible resource management.
  • Make more informed agricultural plans.
  • Improve access to understandable agricultural information.

AGRIHORIZON transforms environmental information into a starting point for better agricultural decisions.

AGRIHORIZON — SEE BEYOND. GROW SMARTER.

04. NASA DATA AND SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION

4.1 The Role of NASA Earth Observations

A strong agricultural decision-support system needs reliable environmental information. Earth-observation programmes provide valuable ways to study temperature, rainfall, land conditions, vegetation and changes in the Earth's environment across different geographic regions.

AGRIHORIZON uses Earth-observation information as part of its approach to understanding agricultural conditions. By connecting environmental information with geographic context, available soil information and crop characteristics, the platform aims to make scientific data more useful for agricultural planning.

NASA's Earth-observation resources are particularly relevant because they provide globally accessible information that can support environmental monitoring, climate analysis and agricultural research.

4.2 NASA POWER: Environmental and Climate Information

One of the NASA resources used in AGRIHORIZON is NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources).

NASA POWER provides solar and meteorological data through services designed to make environmental information accessible to researchers, developers and agricultural applications.

Depending on the selected parameters and location, its data can include:

  • Daily maximum and minimum air temperatures.
  • Precipitation information.
  • Relative humidity.
  • Wind speed.
  • Solar radiation.

Within AGRIHORIZON, NASA POWER provides environmental information that can help users examine temperature and weather-related conditions associated with a selected location.

This information can support environmental monitoring, climate analysis and agricultural planning. It also provides a foundation for exploring how changing environmental conditions may influence farming decisions.

Scientific consideration: NASA POWER provides gridded environmental data derived from observations and scientific analysis. Its values should not be interpreted as direct measurements from a sensor installed on an individual farm.

Figure 4. Earth-observation information for agricultural analysis. Conceptual illustration showing how satellite observations and environmental datasets can provide information about atmospheric conditions, rainfall, land and vegetation to support agricultural decision-making. Illustration by INKINDI TECH.

4.3 Connecting Environmental Data with Agricultural Information

Environmental data becomes more useful when interpreted alongside other relevant agricultural information.

AGRIHORIZON's approach combines several information categories:

Environmental information: Temperature, rainfall and other available climate indicators help describe the conditions affecting an agricultural location.

Geographic information: Location and mapping information help establish the geographic context for environmental analysis.

Soil information: Available soil datasets and local soil information can provide additional context for understanding land characteristics. Their spatial coverage and accuracy must be considered.

Crop characteristics: Crop requirements and growing conditions help users explore whether particular crop options may be suitable for a given environment.

Farmer priorities: Agricultural decisions also depend on individual circumstances, resources and objectives. AGRIHORIZON is designed to consider these priorities when exploring possible strategies.

Bringing these categories together creates a more informed basis for examining crop choices and crop-rotation strategies.

4.4 Complementary Satellite Information

AGRIHORIZON also presents satellite-derived information, including Sentinel-2 imagery, to support geographic and vegetation-related exploration.

Sentinel-2 belongs to the European Space Agency's Copernicus programme, not NASA. It is therefore identified as a complementary non-NASA Earth-observation resource rather than a NASA dataset.

Satellite imagery can help users observe land-cover and vegetation patterns over time. However, vegetation indicators such as NDVI represent vegetation greenness and activity; they do not directly measure soil fertility, nutrient content or crop yield.

Using different sources with clearly identified origins helps AGRIHORIZON provide a broader environmental picture without confusing the organisations responsible for each dataset.

4.5 Opportunities for Additional NASA Data Integration

Several other NASA datasets offer opportunities to expand AGRIHORIZON's scientific capabilities in future development:

NASA GPM IMERG — Precipitation Estimates

The Global Precipitation Measurement mission provides satellite-based precipitation estimates that can help examine rainfall patterns, compare precipitation over time and investigate potential water-related agricultural risks.

NASA Landsat — Land and Vegetation Observation

The Landsat programme provides satellite imagery useful for examining land-cover changes, vegetation patterns and agricultural landscapes over time.

NASA SMAP — Soil Moisture

The Soil Moisture Active Passive mission provides information about soil moisture conditions. These observations can contribute to broader assessments of water availability, but they are not direct measurements of soil nutrients or the exact moisture content of every individual field.

NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 — Future Climate Projections

This dataset provides downscaled climate projections that can support research into possible future temperature and precipitation conditions under different climate scenarios. It could strengthen AGRIHORIZON's longer-term climate adaptation and agricultural planning capabilities.

These datasets are presented as potential future integrations unless their data have been implemented and verified in the current application.

4.6 Scientific Reliability and Data Limitations

AGRIHORIZON recognizes that satellite observations, gridded environmental products and climate models have different spatial resolutions, update frequencies and uncertainties.

For responsible interpretation, the platform should distinguish between:

  • Satellite observations and satellite-derived estimates.
  • Modelled environmental information.
  • Historical records and future climate projections.
  • Regional information and individual farm measurements.
  • Verified information and illustrative demonstration values.

Satellite data cannot replace every form of local agricultural assessment. Soil nutrients, pH and other field-specific characteristics may require laboratory testing or reliable local soil information. Likewise, environmental estimates should not be presented as direct farm sensor readings.

By communicating these distinctions, AGRIHORIZON aims to make scientific information more understandable while respecting the limitations of the underlying data.

The scientific foundation of AGRIHORIZON is built around a simple principle: useful agricultural intelligence must be informed by credible data, transparent about uncertainty and relevant to the location being considered.

05. PLATFORM FEATURES AND PRODUCT DEMONSTRATION

5.1 A Connected Agricultural Intelligence Platform

AGRIHORIZON brings agricultural information, environmental observations and decision-support tools together in one digital platform. Its interface is designed to help farmers explore information about their farms, understand environmental conditions and consider agricultural strategies through a more connected and accessible experience.

Instead of requiring users to interpret multiple complex data sources independently, AGRIHORIZON organizes relevant information into dedicated features that support different stages of agricultural planning.

5.2 Farm Overview and Monitoring

The farm overview provides a central point from which users can explore their agricultural information. It brings together farm-related details and environmental indicators to help users understand the conditions surrounding their agricultural activities.

Through the monitoring interface, users can explore information such as temperature, rainfall and other available environmental indicators. This information can help provide context for agricultural planning and highlight conditions that may deserve closer attention.

5.3 Farm Mapping and Geospatial Intelligence

AGRIHORIZON incorporates a geographical approach to agricultural planning. Its farm-mapping experience helps users connect agricultural information with specific locations and explore the relationship between their farms and the surrounding environment.

Geospatial information can provide useful context for understanding local conditions and interpreting Earth-observation data. The accuracy and detail of the information depend on the underlying datasets, their spatial resolution and their availability for the selected location.

5.4 Farm Intelligence and Environmental Insights

The Farm Intelligence feature brings environmental information into an agricultural context. By presenting relevant climate and land-observation information in an understandable interface, AGRIHORIZON aims to make scientific data more accessible to agricultural users.

The platform's environmental information can support the exploration of temperature, rainfall, vegetation and other relevant indicators, depending on the data source available. NASA POWER and other Earth-observation resources provide opportunities to examine environmental conditions over time and across different locations.

5.5 Crop and Rotation Planner

The Crop and Rotation Planner addresses an important part of the NASA Field Shift challenge: exploring crop choices and rotation strategies in response to changing environmental conditions and soil-health considerations.

The feature is intended to help users compare agricultural options by considering relevant factors such as environmental conditions, crop characteristics, available soil information and farmer priorities.

Rather than presenting one crop choice as universally correct, AGRIHORIZON aims to support the comparison of possible strategies. Actual recommendations depend on the quality and availability of the information provided, and should be considered alongside local agricultural knowledge and expert advice.

5.6 AI Farm Advisor

The AI Farm Advisor is designed to make agricultural information easier to understand and use. It provides an interactive way for users to explore agricultural questions and receive guidance based on the information available to the platform.

Its purpose is to help translate complex information into clearer explanations and practical considerations. AI-generated guidance should be treated as decision-support information, not a substitute for verified scientific data, local agricultural expertise or professional advice.

5.7 Alerts, Guidance and Farmer Learning

AGRIHORIZON also aims to make agricultural information more useful beyond the initial planning stage.

Its alerts and guidance experience is intended to help users pay attention to relevant environmental changes and potential agricultural risks. The learning component supports access to understandable agricultural information and encourages continued learning.

Together, these features reflect AGRIHORIZON's wider objective: connecting environmental understanding with informed agricultural decisions.

5.8 Designed Around the Farmer

The platform is being developed with accessibility and usability in mind. Agricultural intelligence should not be limited to users with advanced technical knowledge. AGRIHORIZON therefore aims to present information through a clear interface, understandable explanations and tools organized around practical farming questions.

By bringing monitoring, mapping, environmental intelligence, crop planning and AI-assisted guidance into one experience, AGRIHORIZON seeks to make Earth-observation information more approachable and relevant to farming communities.

06. HOW AGRIHORIZON WORKS

6.1 From Earth Observations to Agricultural Decisions

AGRIHORIZON follows an integrated approach that connects environmental information with agricultural context. Its purpose is to make relevant information easier to explore and use when considering farm-management strategies.

The process begins with information about a selected location and its surrounding environment. Earth-observation and climate datasets can provide insights into environmental conditions, while available soil information and crop characteristics add important agricultural context.

AGRIHORIZON brings these information sources together within a digital decision-support experience, helping users explore possible agricultural strategies and understand the factors that may influence their decisions. Figure 9. AGRIHORIZON's decision-support workflow. Conceptual illustration developed by INKINDI TECH, showing how farm location, Earth-observation information, available agricultural data and farmer priorities can be connected to support informed crop-planning decisions.

6.2 Step One: Understanding the Farm's Location

The first step is establishing the geographical context of the agricultural area being explored. Farm location provides an important reference for connecting environmental datasets with the relevant region.

Geographical information helps the platform identify which location-based observations and datasets may be relevant. The usefulness of the resulting insights depends on the accuracy of the selected location and the spatial coverage of the available data.

6.3 Step Two: Exploring Environmental Conditions

The platform uses available environmental information to help users explore conditions such as temperature, rainfall and other relevant indicators.

NASA Earth-observation resources can contribute information about weather, climate, rainfall, land and vegetation. These observations help establish a broader picture of environmental conditions and how they may change over time.

It is important to recognize that satellite and gridded datasets do not necessarily represent direct measurements from an individual farm. Their spatial resolution, observation periods and uncertainties must be considered when interpreting the results.

6.4 Step Three: Connecting Agricultural Information

Environmental information becomes more meaningful when considered alongside agricultural context.

AGRIHORIZON's approach incorporates available soil information, crop characteristics and farmer-defined priorities into the planning process. These factors help users consider why a particular crop or rotation strategy may be more suitable under certain conditions.

Soil information may include properties such as texture, pH and nutrient status when reliable data are available. Satellite observations alone cannot establish all soil properties, and field testing remains important for obtaining accurate information about individual farms.

6.5 Step Four: Exploring Crop and Rotation Strategies

The Crop and Rotation Planner is intended to help users examine possible crop choices and rotation strategies using the information available to the platform.

This stage considers the relationship between environmental conditions, crop requirements, soil considerations and farmer priorities. Users can explore alternatives rather than relying on a single recommendation.

Crop rotation is particularly important because different crops interact with soil and agricultural systems in different ways. Appropriate rotations can contribute to soil-health management, diversification and adaptation, depending on local conditions and agricultural practices.

6.6 Step Five: Turning Information into Understandable Guidance

The final stage is presenting agricultural information in a form that users can understand and consider.

AGRIHORIZON's interface, planning tools and AI-assisted advisor are intended to help users interpret information, explore alternatives and identify questions that may require further investigation.

The result is a decision-support experience that connects scientific information with agricultural planning. It is designed to assist farmers and other users in making more informed decisions, while recognizing that recommendations must be evaluated against local conditions and expert agricultural knowledge.

6.7 A Continuous Learning Approach

Agricultural conditions are not static. Temperature, rainfall, soil conditions, crop performance and farmer priorities can change over time.

AGRIHORIZON therefore aims to support an ongoing process of observation, interpretation and planning. As additional datasets, local information and validated agricultural knowledge become available, the platform can be expanded to provide more relevant and comprehensive decision support.

The central idea is simple: connect information about the planet with information about the farm, then make that knowledge easier to use in agricultural decisions.

07. TECHNOLOGY AND DEVELOPMENT

7.1 Development Approach

AGRIHORIZON was developed as a web-based agricultural decision-support platform by INKINDI TECH. The development process focused on creating an accessible digital experience that brings agricultural information, environmental intelligence and decision-support features into one interface.

The team adopted an iterative development approach, using AI-assisted development tools to explore the concept, structure the platform, design its interface and develop its features. This approach allowed the team to move from an initial idea towards a working web-based demonstration while exploring how Earth-observation information could be made more understandable and useful for agricultural planning.

7.2 Platform and Development Tools

The platform was developed using Google AI Studio as an AI-assisted development environment. It supported the process of translating design requirements and written development instructions into the web application's interface and functionality.

The development process also involved designing the platform's visual identity, organizing its pages and components, and refining the user experience to create a consistent agricultural technology platform.

The technologies and services used in the final implementation should be identified according to the actual published application's source code and configuration.

7.3 User Interface and Experience

AGRIHORIZON's interface is designed around clarity, accessibility and ease of navigation. Its visual approach combines agricultural themes with a modern scientific and geospatial design language.

The platform organizes its features into dedicated experiences, including farm monitoring, mapping, environmental intelligence, crop planning and AI-assisted guidance. This structure is intended to help users move from understanding environmental information towards exploring agricultural decisions.

7.4 AI-Assisted Development and Agricultural Guidance

Artificial intelligence played a role in the development process and in the platform's proposed agricultural guidance experience.

During development, AI-assisted tools helped the team explore interface designs, refine instructions and accelerate the creation of digital components. Within the platform, the AI Farm Advisor is intended to help users interpret agricultural information and explore relevant questions.

AI-generated information is not treated as a replacement for scientific observations, validated datasets or professional agricultural expertise. The reliability of agricultural guidance depends on the quality of the information available to the platform.

7.5 Data Integration and Platform Architecture

AGRIHORIZON is designed around the connection of geographical information, environmental datasets and agricultural knowledge.

Its intended architecture allows relevant information to be organized and presented through a unified web interface. Data sources may provide different types of information, including climate indicators, rainfall estimates, land observations and agricultural characteristics.

The platform's architecture can be expanded as additional datasets, validated agricultural information and backend capabilities become available. Any data source described as currently integrated should correspond to a connection that is operational in the submitted demonstration.

7.6 Development Challenges and Learning

Developing AGRIHORIZON involved exploring how complex environmental information could be translated into a practical agricultural experience.

The team had to consider the differences between satellite observations, gridded environmental datasets and measurements collected directly in the field. It was also important to consider data availability, geographic coverage, scientific limitations and the need to communicate uncertainty clearly.

Working with AI-assisted development tools provided an opportunity to experiment, refine the platform and develop a more structured understanding of agricultural technology.

7.7 Future Technical Development

Future development opportunities include expanding validated data integrations, strengthening backend and database capabilities, improving multilingual accessibility, supporting offline access and developing more comprehensive crop and rotation analysis.

These improvements could help AGRIHORIZON evolve from its current demonstration into a more comprehensive agricultural decision-support platform for farming communities across different regions. 08. INNOVATION AND GLOBAL ADAPTABILITY

8.1 Beyond Traditional Farm Monitoring

Many digital agricultural tools focus on displaying weather information, monitoring individual farm conditions or providing general agricultural advice. AGRIHORIZON takes a broader approach by bringing environmental information and agricultural planning into one connected experience.

Its central innovation is the idea of connecting Earth-observation information with geographical farm context, available soil information, crop characteristics and farmer-defined priorities.

Rather than simply showing environmental indicators, AGRIHORIZON aims to help users explore what those indicators may mean for agricultural planning and possible crop-rotation strategies.

8.2 Connecting Multiple Dimensions of Agricultural Decision-Making

AGRIHORIZON's approach recognizes that agricultural decisions are influenced by several interconnected factors.

Temperature and rainfall conditions affect crop development and agricultural planning. Soil properties influence crop suitability and soil-management decisions. Crop characteristics help determine which agricultural options may be appropriate, while farmer priorities provide important practical context.

By bringing these dimensions together, AGRIHORIZON provides a framework for exploring agricultural strategies from a more integrated perspective.

8.3 Making Scientific Information More Accessible

Earth-observation datasets contain valuable scientific information, but interpreting them can be challenging for users without technical or scientific backgrounds.

AGRIHORIZON seeks to reduce this barrier by organizing environmental information into understandable visualizations, agricultural indicators and interactive decision-support experiences.

Its AI-assisted advisor is intended to help users explore agricultural questions and interpret available information in clearer language.

The wider goal is to make scientific information more approachable without removing the scientific limitations or uncertainty associated with the underlying datasets.

8.4 Supporting Climate-Smart Crop Planning

A major aspect of AGRIHORIZON's innovation is its focus on crop choices and rotation strategies under changing environmental conditions.

Users can explore agricultural alternatives while considering environmental information, crop characteristics, available soil information and their own priorities.

This approach supports the exploration of strategies that may contribute to soil-health management, agricultural diversification and climate adaptation.

It also reflects an important principle: agricultural recommendations should consider the interaction between crops, soil and environmental conditions rather than relying on a single indicator.

8.5 Designed for Different Agricultural Regions

AGRIHORIZON is designed with a global perspective. Agricultural communities across the world experience different climates, soil conditions, farming systems and environmental pressures.

The platform's approach can be adapted to different geographical locations by using relevant regional datasets, locally appropriate crop information and agricultural knowledge.

For example, users in regions affected by irregular rainfall may prioritize water availability and drought preparedness, while users in areas experiencing changing temperature patterns may explore different crop suitability and rotation considerations.

The platform is not restricted to one country or farming system. Its wider potential depends on the availability and quality of location-specific data and the inclusion of relevant local agricultural knowledge.

8.6 A Foundation for Future Agricultural Innovation

AGRIHORIZON provides a foundation that can be expanded through additional validated datasets, improved agricultural models, multilingual support and stronger local partnerships.

Future development could include more detailed crop-suitability analysis, improved soil-health assessment, additional climate scenarios and more comprehensive agricultural decision-support capabilities.

Through this approach, AGRIHORIZON aims to contribute to a future in which Earth-observation information becomes more accessible, understandable and useful for agricultural communities worldwide. 09. EXPECTED IMPACT AND BENEFITS TO FARMERS

9.1 Supporting More Informed Agricultural Decisions

Agricultural decisions are influenced by environmental conditions, soil characteristics, crop requirements and available resources. However, accessing and interpreting this information can be difficult, particularly when relevant information is distributed across different sources.

AGRIHORIZON aims to make this process easier by bringing environmental and agricultural information into one decision-support experience.

By helping users explore relevant conditions and compare possible agricultural strategies, the platform seeks to encourage more informed planning and reduce reliance on decisions made without sufficient environmental context.

9.2 Contributing to Soil Health and Sustainable Crop Rotation

Healthy soils are essential for productive and resilient agricultural systems. However, soil degradation, nutrient depletion and unsuitable land-management practices can threaten long-term agricultural sustainability.

AGRIHORIZON addresses this concern through its focus on crop planning and rotation exploration.

By connecting available soil information with crop characteristics and environmental conditions, the platform aims to help users consider crop sequences and agricultural practices that may support soil-health management.

Appropriate crop rotations can contribute to diversification, nutrient management and the interruption of certain pest and disease cycles. Their suitability depends on local soil conditions, crop requirements and management practices.

9.3 Strengthening Climate Adaptation and Preparedness

Changing temperature and rainfall patterns create challenges for agricultural communities across different regions.

AGRIHORIZON aims to help users explore environmental information that may be relevant to agricultural planning and climate adaptation.

Access to climate indicators and Earth-observation information can help users examine changing conditions, consider potential risks and explore alternative crop-planning strategies.

The platform's longer-term potential includes supporting the comparison of agricultural options under different environmental and climate scenarios.

9.4 Improving Access to Agricultural Information

Access to useful agricultural information should not be limited to people with advanced technical knowledge or access to specialized scientific tools.

AGRIHORIZON aims to make environmental and agricultural information easier to understand through organized dashboards, visual explanations and AI-assisted guidance.

Its future development opportunities include improved multilingual support and more accessible learning experiences, helping users with different educational and technological backgrounds engage with agricultural information.

9.5 Supporting Farmers, Communities and Agricultural Stakeholders

The potential value of AGRIHORIZON extends beyond individual farm decisions.

Farmers may use the platform to explore agricultural conditions and planning alternatives. Agricultural advisers and educators could use it as an additional information resource. Researchers and other agricultural stakeholders may find opportunities to explore the relationship between environmental observations and agricultural systems.

The platform's wider value will depend on reliable data, local validation and collaboration with agricultural communities and experts.

9.6 Long-Term Environmental and Socioeconomic Potential

By encouraging more informed crop planning, soil-conscious agricultural practices and climate preparedness, AGRIHORIZON aims to contribute to more resilient agricultural systems.

Potential long-term benefits include improved consideration of soil health, more informed resource management, greater awareness of environmental risks and stronger agricultural decision-making.

These benefits are intended outcomes rather than measured impacts at the current prototype stage. Demonstrating actual improvements in soil conditions, productivity, farmer income or resilience will require field testing, farmer feedback and evaluation over time.

9.7 Our Vision for the Future

AGRIHORIZON seeks to help transform Earth-observation information into knowledge that can support real agricultural decisions.

Our ambition is to make agricultural intelligence more accessible and useful across different farming environments, helping communities better understand their land, respond to environmental change and explore sustainable agricultural strategies.

We believe that the future of agriculture requires not only better information, but also better ways of turning that information into meaningful action.10. LIMITATIONS, FUTURE DEVELOPMENT AND REFERENCES

10.1 Current Limitations

AGRIHORIZON is a developing agricultural decision-support platform. Although its current demonstration establishes the concept and brings together several agricultural information experiences, some capabilities require further development, testing and validation.

Earth-observation datasets have different spatial resolutions, observation periods and levels of uncertainty. Consequently, satellite-derived or gridded environmental information may not represent the exact conditions of an individual farm.

Similarly, the availability and accuracy of soil information can vary between locations. Satellite observations cannot independently establish every soil property, including detailed nutrient concentrations and soil ph. Reliable field measurements and soil testing remain important.

AI-assisted agricultural guidance also has limitations. Generated information may be incomplete or unsuitable for particular local conditions. It therefore requires careful interpretation and should not replace qualified agricultural advice.

The current platform should be understood as a decision-support demonstration rather than a fully validated agricultural prediction system. Its recommendations and potential benefits require further evaluation using reliable data and real-world agricultural feedback.

10.2 Future Development

Future development will focus on improving the platform's scientific foundation, technical capabilities and practical usefulness.

Key development priorities include:

  • Expanded NASA data integration: Incorporating additional relevant Earth-observation datasets, including rainfall, land-surface and soil-moisture information where appropriate.
  • Improved crop and rotation analysis: Developing more comprehensive methods for comparing crop characteristics, environmental suitability and rotation strategies.
  • Better soil information: Connecting reliable soil datasets and supporting the inclusion of field-based soil-test results.
  • Climate scenario exploration: Expanding the use of climate projections to help users examine possible future agricultural conditions.
  • Multilingual accessibility: Improving language support and making agricultural information easier to understand for users with different educational backgrounds.
  • Offline functionality: Exploring access to essential information and learning materials where internet connectivity is limited.
  • Field testing and validation: Working with farmers, agricultural specialists and relevant institutions to test the platform and improve its usefulness.
  • Stronger technical infrastructure: Improving data management, platform reliability, security and backend capabilities as the project develops.

10.3 Validation and Real-World Evaluation

The effectiveness of AGRIHORIZON must ultimately be assessed through practical use and scientific evaluation.

Future testing could examine the accuracy and usefulness of environmental information, the relevance of crop-planning suggestions, the clarity of the user experience and the platform's ability to support agricultural decision-making.

Feedback from farmers and agricultural experts will be important for identifying limitations, improving recommendations and ensuring that the platform responds to real agricultural needs.

Potential long-term evaluation indicators could include user understanding of environmental information, the usefulness of crop-rotation comparisons, adoption of soil-conscious practices and changes in agricultural planning.

Any claims about improved yields, soil health or farmer income will require appropriate field evidence over time.

10.4 Conclusion

AGRIHORIZON was developed in response to the challenge of making Earth-observation information more accessible and useful for agricultural adaptation.

By connecting environmental observations with geographical context, available soil information, crop characteristics and farmer priorities, the platform explores how digital technology can support more informed agricultural planning and crop-rotation decisions.

Its development reflects our belief that scientific information becomes more valuable when it can be understood and applied to real-world challenges.

Although further development, validation and collaboration are necessary, AGRIHORIZON provides a foundation for exploring how agricultural intelligence can contribute to more sustainable and climate-resilient farming systems.

Data Interpretation and Limitations

AGRIHORIZON recognizes that satellite observations and gridded environmental datasets provide information at different spatial and temporal resolutions. They do not automatically represent the exact conditions of every individual farm. Soil-property maps are modelled estimates and should not replace laboratory soil testing or field assessment. Vegetation indicators should not be interpreted as direct measurements of soil fertility or crop yield.

The platform's future development will focus on expanding data integration, improving local validation, strengthening agricultural recommendations and making scientific information more accessible to farming communities in different regions.
